correctness.rationale: The full antipodal Walsh character basis gives the finite eigenvalue formula and exact multiplicities. The fractional-cosine integral, with its convergent near-zero integrand for 2k>p, and a pair-of-half-periods argument show strict positivity for every residual cosine exponent, including odd. Thus all nonconstant eigenvalues have sign (-1)^{k+1} and the constant level is strictly positive. The resulting linear system forces exact signs-only quadrature weights, and p=2 follows by quadratic expansion. A standalone standard-library checker executed 587 finite diagnostics, independent of the infinite analytic proof.
